title.zh: 第二十四 百官一 太傅 太尉 司徒 司空 將軍
title.raw: 第二十四 百官一 太傅 太尉 司徒 司空 將軍 Volume 114: Officials Part One

sentences.zh: 志第二十四 百官一

translations.literal: Treatise twenty-four: Officials, Part One.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 24: Officials, Part One.

sentences.zh: 太傅 太尉 司徒 司空 将军

translations.literal: Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, Minister of Works, General.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor, the Grand Commandant, the Minister of Education, the Minister of Works, and the generalship.

sentences.zh: 汉之初兴，承继大乱，兵不及戢，法度草创，略依秦制，后嗣因循。

translations.literal: When Han first arose, it followed upon great chaos; the troops had no time to be laid aside; laws and institutions were rudimentarily created; it roughly followed Qin institutions, and later rulers carried them on.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty emerged from utter turmoil: the armies had scarcely been stood down when statutes and offices were framed in haste, largely on Qin models, and succeeding reigns largely left that pattern in place.

sentences.zh: 至景帝，感吴楚之难，始抑损诸侯王。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Jing, moved by the disaster of Wu and Chu, he began to curtail the feudal kings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, sobered by the revolt of Wu and Chu, began to pare back the power of the feudal kings.

sentences.zh: 及至武帝，多所改作，然而奢广，民用匮乏。

translations.literal: When it reached Emperor Wu, there were many changes and new creations, yet there was extravagance and expansion, and the people's resources were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu refashioned much of the machinery of state, but that age's breadth and lavish spending drained the common people.

sentences.zh: 世祖中兴，务从节约，并官省职，费减亿计，所以补复残缺，及身未改，而四海从风，中国安乐者也。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor's restoration practiced compliance with thrift, merging offices and reducing posts; expenditures decreased by sums reckoned in the hundreds of millions; by this means patching and restoring what was broken and incomplete; throughout his life he did not alter it, yet within the Four Seas they followed like the wind, and the Central States were peaceful and happy.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu restored the Han, he enforced austerity, merged bureaus and cut posts, and saved sums on the order of hundreds of millions of cash, mending what the wars had shattered. He held that course for life, and the realm fell into step; the heartland knew peace again.

sentences.zh: 昔周公作《周官》，分职著明，法度相持，王室虽微，犹能久存。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou made the "Offices of Zhou," dividing duties so they were clear and manifest; laws and institutions supported one another; though the royal house was weak, still it was able to endure long.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Duke of Zhou set down the Rites of Zhou, with every duty spelled out and institutions buttressing one another, so that even as royal power thinned, the dynasty endured.

sentences.zh: 今其遗书，所以观周室牧民之德既至，又其有益来事之范，殆未有所穷也。

translations.literal: Now its surviving documents, whereby one may observe that the Zhou house's virtue in shepherding the people had reached the utmost, and also that their model is beneficial to later affairs, probably cannot be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: What survives of that text still shows how thoroughly Zhou rule tended the people and offers a pattern for later ages that admits no easy final word.

sentences.zh: 故新汲令王隆作《小学汉官篇》，诸文倜说，较略不究。

translations.literal: Therefore the magistrate of Xinji, Wang Long, composed the "Elementary Learning Han Offices Chapter"; the various texts were divergent and explanatory, comparatively summary and not thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Wang Long, once magistrate of Xinji, composed the Elementary Han Offices—a work that wanders and abbreviates rather than exhausting the subject.

sentences.zh: 唯班固著《百官公卿表》，记汉承秦置官本末，讫于王莽，差有条贯；

translations.literal: Only Ban Gu wrote the "Table of All Offices and Nobles," recording from beginning to end Han's inheriting Qin's establishment of offices, down to Wang Mang, somewhat having order and continuity;
translations.idiomatic: Only Ban Gu's Table of Officials and Nobles traced how Han took over Qin offices from start to finish, down to Wang Mang, with something like a clear thread;

sentences.zh: 然皆孝武奢广之事，又职分未悉。

translations.literal: yet they are all matters of Emperor Wu's extravagance and expansion, moreover duties and divisions of office were not fully detailed.
translations.idiomatic: yet his focus falls on Emperor Wu's expansion and luxury, and the boundaries of each post remain incompletely spelled out.

sentences.zh: 世祖节约之制，宜为常宪，故依其官簿，粗注职分，以为《百官志》。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor's system of thrift ought to be the constant statute; therefore relying on his roster of offices, coarsely annotating duties and divisions, making it the "Treatise on Officials."
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu's lean institutions deserve to stand as the enduring norm; this treatise follows his official register and sketches each post's remit—hence this Treatise on Officials.

sentences.zh: 凡置官之本及中兴所省，无因复见者，既在《汉书·百官表》，不复悉载。

translations.literal: As for the root of establishing offices and what the restoration abolished, what has no cause to appear again, since it is already in the Hanshu "Table of Officials," is not again fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Foundations of the bureaucracy and cuts made at the restoration that need no second telling already sit in the Hanshu table of offices, so they are not repeated here in full.

sentences.zh: 太傅，上公一人。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor: supreme duke, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor: one holder among the supreme dukes.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌以善导，无常职。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he leads by good guidance; there are no fixed duties.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He guides the sovereign toward good conduct and has no fixed portfolio.

sentences.zh: 世祖以卓茂为太傅，薨，因省。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor appointed Zhuo Mao as Grand Tutor; when he died, therefore it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu named Zhuo Mao Grand Tutor; when Zhuo died, the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 其后每帝初即位，辄置太傅录尚书事，薨，辄省。

translations.literal: After that, whenever each emperor first ascended the throne, he always established a Grand Tutor to record Masters of Writing affairs; when he died, it was always abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter each new sovereign would appoint a Grand Tutor to oversee the Masters of Writing; when that man died, the office vanished again.

sentences.zh: 太尉，公一人。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant: duke, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant: one at the rank of duke.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌四方兵事功课，岁尽即奏其殿最而行赏罚。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds military affairs in the four directions and merit assessment; when the year ends he reports the lowest and highest rankings and carries out rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He directs military affairs across the realm and, at year's end, ranks the regions for reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 凡郊祀之事，掌亚献；

translations.literal: In matters of suburban sacrifice, he presents the second libation;
translations.idiomatic: At suburban sacrifices he presents the second libation;

sentences.zh: 大丧则告谥南郊。

translations.literal: in great mourning he proclaims the posthumous title at the southern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: on a great imperial death he proclaims the posthumous title at the southern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 凡国有大造大疑，则与司徒、司空通而论之。

translations.literal: Whenever the state has great undertakings or great doubts, then with the Minister of Education and the Minister of Works he jointly discusses them.
translations.idiomatic: On momentous policy or unresolved state matters he deliberates jointly with the Minister of Education and the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 国有过事，则与二公通谏争之。

translations.literal: If the state has faulty affairs, then with the two dukes he jointly remonstrates and contends.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign errs, he joins the other two dukes in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，为大司马。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor, when ascending the throne, was Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu took power as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 建武二十七年，改为太尉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu, it was changed to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 27 (51 CE) it became the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 长史一人，千石。

translations.literal: Chief clerk: one person, one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One chief clerk at one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：署诸曹事。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he administers the affairs of the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He runs day-to-day affairs of the bureaus.

sentences.zh: 掾史属二十四人。

translations.literal: Attendant clerks and subordinates: twenty-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four attendant clerks and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：《汉旧注》东西曹掾比四百石，余掾比三百石，属比二百石，故曰公府掾，比古元士三命者也。

translations.literal: Original commentary: the Han Old Commentary states that East and West Bureau attendants are comparable to four hundred bushels, the remaining attendants comparable to three hundred bushels, subordinates comparable to two hundred bushels; therefore they are called ducal-mansion attendants, comparable to the ancient primordial scholars of three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Per the Old Han Commentary: East and West Bureau attendants rank at four hundred bushels equivalent, other attendants at three hundred, subordinates at two hundred—collectively the ducal mansion staff, likened to antiquity's three-ranked primordial scholar.

sentences.zh: 或曰，汉初掾史辟，皆上言之，故有秩比命士，其所不言，则为百石属。

translations.literal: Someone says: at the beginning of Han, attendant clerks' recruitment was all reported upward; therefore there were ranks comparable to ordained scholars; what was not thus reported was hundred-bushel subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that under the early Han, nominated clerks were reported to the throne, so grades matched the ordained scholar; unreported cases counted as hundred-bushel subordinates.

sentences.zh: 其后皆自辟除，故通为百石云。

translations.literal: After that they were all self-recruited and dismissed; therefore generally they were hundred bushels, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were hired directly by the minister, and the rank settled at one hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 西曹主府史署用。

translations.literal: The West Bureau masters appointment and use of mansion clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The West Bureau handles appointments of mansion clerks.

sentences.zh: 东曹主二千石长史迁除及军吏。

translations.literal: The East Bureau masters promotion and removal of two-thousand-bushel chief clerks and of military clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The East Bureau handles promotions and transfers of two-thousand-bushel chief clerks and of military officers.

sentences.zh: 户曹主民户、祠祀、农桑。

translations.literal: The Household Bureau masters household registers, shrine sacrifice, agriculture and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: The Household Bureau covers population registers, sacrificial rites, and farming and silk production.

sentences.zh: 奏曹主奏议事。

translations.literal: The Memorial Bureau masters memorials and deliberation of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Memorial Bureau drafts and debates memorials.

sentences.zh: 辞曹主辞讼事。

translations.literal: The Petitions Bureau masters petitions and lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: The Petitions Bureau handles litigation and written plaints.

sentences.zh: 法曹主邮驿科程事。

translations.literal: The Law Bureau masters post relays, statutes, and procedural schedules.
translations.idiomatic: The Law Bureau oversees courier posts, statutory rules, and procedural deadlines.

sentences.zh: 尉曹主卒徒转运事。

translations.literal: The Commandant Bureau masters conscripts, convicts, transport, and transfer.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant Bureau manages transport by soldiers and conscript laborers.

sentences.zh: 贼曹主盗贼事。

translations.literal: The Bandit Bureau masters bandits and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: The Bandit Bureau pursues robbery and theft.

sentences.zh: 决曹主罪法事。

translations.literal: The Judgment Bureau masters crimes and law.
translations.idiomatic: The Judgment Bureau handles criminal law.

sentences.zh: 兵曹主兵事。

translations.literal: The Military Bureau masters military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau oversees army matters.

sentences.zh: 金曹主货币、盐、铁事。

translations.literal: The Metal Bureau masters currency, salt, and iron.
translations.idiomatic: The Metal Bureau handles coinage, salt, and iron.

sentences.zh: 仓曹主仓谷事。

translations.literal: The Granary Bureau masters granaries and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Bureau manages state granaries.

sentences.zh: 黄阁主簿录省从事。

translations.literal: The Yellow Gate chief clerk records and checks provincial attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Gate chief clerk keeps the roster of provincial staff.

sentences.zh: 令史及御属二十三人。

translations.literal: Clerks and ministerial attendants: twenty-three persons.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-three clerks and ministerial attendants.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：《汉旧注》公令史百石，自中兴以后，注不说石数。

translations.literal: Original commentary: the Han Old Commentary states ducal clerks at one hundred bushels; from the restoration onward the commentary does not state bushel numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The Old Han Commentary gives ducal clerks at one hundred bushels; after the restoration the figure is left unstated.

sentences.zh: 御属主为公卿。

translations.literal: Ministerial attendants act on behalf of the dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Ministerial attendants serve as liaisons for the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 阁下令史主阁下威仪事。

translations.literal: Lower-pavilion clerks master ceremony and order below the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Pavilion clerks manage ceremony and order below the hall.

sentences.zh: 记室令史主上章表报书记。

translations.literal: The records-chamber clerks master submitting memorials, tables, reports, and correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat clerks draft memorials, bulletins, and correspondence.

sentences.zh: 门令史主府门。

translations.literal: Gate clerks master the mansion gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gate clerks guard the ministry's outer doors.

sentences.zh: 其余令史，各典曹文书。

translations.literal: The remaining clerks each manage bureau documents.
translations.idiomatic: Other clerks each keep their bureau's paperwork.

sentences.zh: 司徒，公一人。

translations.literal: Minister of Education: duke, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education: one at duke rank.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌人民事。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds the people's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He oversees matters concerning the people.

sentences.zh: 凡教民孝悌、逊顺、谦俭，养生送死之事，则议其制，建其度。

translations.literal: As for teaching the people filiality and fraternal duty, yielding and compliance, modesty and thrift, and matters of nurturing life and sending off the dead, then he discusses their regulations and establishes their measures.
translations.idiomatic: He frames policy for teaching filial piety, brotherly deference, humility, frugality, and for the people's welfare from birth to burial.

sentences.zh: 凡四方民事功课，岁尽则奏其殿最而行赏罚。

translations.literal: As for civil merit assessment in the four directions, when the year ends he reports the lowest and highest and carries out rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He ranks regional civil administration yearly for rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 凡郊祀之事，掌省牲视氵翟，大丧则掌奉安梓宫。

translations.literal: In matters of suburban sacrifice, he inspects the victim and inspects the washing of vessels; in great mourning he presents and settles the catalpa palace-coffin.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban rites he inspects the sacrificial animal and the cleansing of vessels; at a state funeral he escorts and sets the imperial coffin.

sentences.zh: 凡国有大疑大事，与太尉同。

translations.literal: Whenever the state has great doubt or great affairs, it is the same as the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Great crises and weighty decisions mirror the Grand Commandant's role.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，为大司徒，建武二十七年，去「大」。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor, when ascending the throne, was Grand Minister of Education; in the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu the word "grand" was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu began as Grand Minister of Education; Jianwu 27 dropped the prefix "grand."

sentences.zh: 长史一人，千石。

translations.literal: Chief clerk: one person, one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One chief clerk at one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 掾属三十一人。

translations.literal: Attendants and subordinates: thirty-one persons.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-one attendants and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 令史及御属三十六人。

translations.literal: Clerks and ministerial attendants: thirty-six persons.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-six clerks and ministerial attendants.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：世祖即位，以武帝故事置司直，居丞相府，助督录诸州，建武十八年省也。

translations.literal: Original commentary: the Founding Ancestor, when ascending the throne, by Emperor Wu's precedent established the Straightener, residing in the chancellor's mansion, assisting in supervising and recording the various provinces; in the eighteenth year of Jianwu it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu revived Emperor Wu's office of the Straightener in the chancellor's compound to help supervise the provinces; it was cut in Jianwu 18.

sentences.zh: 司空，公一人。

translations.literal: Minister of Works: duke, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works: one at duke rank.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌水土事。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds water and earth affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He is in charge of public works and hydraulic projects.

sentences.zh: 凡营城起邑、浚沟洫、修坟防之事，则议其利，建其功。

translations.literal: Whenever there are matters of building walls and raising towns, dredging ditches and canals, or repairing mounds and dikes, then he discusses their benefit and establishes their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Walled cities, ditches, dikes, and levees come under his planning for utility and success.

sentences.zh: 凡四方水土功课，岁尽则奏其殿最而行赏罚。

translations.literal: As for water-and-earth merit assessment in the four directions, when the year ends he reports the lowest and highest and carries out rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He annually ranks regional hydraulic and earthworks performance.

sentences.zh: 凡郊祀之事，掌扫除、乐器，大丧则掌将校复土。

translations.literal: In matters of suburban sacrifice, he holds sweeping and cleaning and ritual instruments; in great mourning he leads generals and colonels in back-filling the grave.
translations.idiomatic: He oversees purification, ritual music, and, at imperial burial, directs generals and colonels in the grave-filling rite.

sentences.zh: 凡国有大造大疑，谏争，与太尉同。

translations.literal: Whenever the state has great undertakings or great doubts, remonstrance and contention are the same as the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On great projects and doubts he joins the Grand Commandant in debate and remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，为大司空，建武二十七年，去「大」。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor, when ascending the throne, was Grand Minister of Works; in the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu the word "grand" was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu opened as Grand Minister of Works; Jianwu 27 shortened the title.

sentences.zh: 属长史一人，千石。

translations.literal: Subordinate chief clerk: one person, one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: He has one subordinate chief clerk at one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 掾属二十九人。

translations.literal: Attendants and subordinates: twenty-nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-nine attendants and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 令史及御属四十二人。

translations.literal: Clerks and ministerial attendants: forty-two persons.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-two clerks and ministerial attendants.

sentences.zh: 将军，不常置。

translations.literal: General: not constantly established.
translations.idiomatic: The generalship is not a standing appointment.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌征伐背叛。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds campaigns against rebellion and treason.
translations.idiomatic: He commands punitive expeditions against rebellion.

sentences.zh: 比公者四：第一大将军，次骠骑将军，次车骑将军，次卫将军。

translations.literal: Those comparable to a duke are four: first the Grand General, next the Charging Cavalry General, next the Chariots and Cavalry General, next the Guards General.
translations.idiomatic: Four commands rank with the three dukes: Grand General first, then Palace Charging Cavalry, then Chariots and Cavalry, then Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 又有前、后、左、右将军。

translations.literal: Moreover there are Front, Rear, Left, and Right generals.
translations.idiomatic: There are also Front, Rear, Left, and Right generals.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝以卫青数征伐有功，以为大将军，欲尊宠之。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wu, because Wei Qing repeatedly on campaigns had merit, made him Grand General, desiring to honor and favor him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu first made Wei Qing Grand General to reward his repeated victories and signal his eminence.

sentences.zh: 以古尊官唯有三公，皆将军始自秦、晋，以为卿号，故置大司马官号以冠之。

translations.literal: Because in antiquity the honored offices were only the three dukes, while generals beginning from Qin and Jin were taken as minister titles, therefore he established the Grand Marshal official title to crown them.
translations.idiomatic: Traditionally only the three dukes held supreme civil rank; generalships came from Qin and Jin as minister-level commands, so the court added the Grand Marshal title to crown that authority.

sentences.zh: 其后霍光、王凤等皆然。

translations.literal: After that Huo Guang, Wang Feng, and others were all thus.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huo Guang, Wang Feng, and others held the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 成帝绥和元年，赐大司马印绶，罢将军官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Cheng's Suihe era, he bestowed the Grand Marshal seal and ribbons and abolished the general's office.
translations.idiomatic: In Suhe 1 (8 BCE) Emperor Cheng granted the Grand Marshal insignia and dropped the separate general's title.

sentences.zh: 世祖中兴，吴汉以大将军为大司马，景丹为骠骑大将军，位在公下，及前、后、左、右杂号将军众多，皆主征伐，事讫皆罢。

translations.literal: At the Founding Ancestor's restoration, Wu Han took Grand General as Grand Marshal; Jing Dan was Charging Cavalry Grand General, his position below a duke; and Front, Rear, Left, Right, and miscellaneous-title generals were numerous, all mastering campaigns; when the affairs were finished all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangwu's restoration Wu Han held Grand General merged with Grand Marshal; Jing Dan was Palace Charging Cavalry Grand General, still below ducal rank; many Front, Rear, Left, Right, and miscellaneous generals led field armies only to be disbanded when the fighting ended.

sentences.zh: 明帝初即位，以弟东平王苍有贤才，以为骠骑将军；

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first ascended the throne, because his younger brother the Prince of Dongping, Cang, had worthy talent, he made him Charging Cavalry General;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, seeing talent in his brother Prince Cang of Dongping, first named him Palace Charging Cavalry General;

sentences.zh: 以王故，位在公上，数年后罢。

translations.literal: because he was a king, his position was above a duke; after several years it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: his princely blood lifted him above the dukes until the office was dropped a few years later.

sentences.zh: 章帝即位，西羌反，故以舅马防行车骑将军征之，还后罢。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhang ascended the throne, the Western Qiang rebelled; therefore by his maternal uncle Ma Fang as acting Chariots and Cavalry General he campaigned against them; after returning it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Qiang rose under Emperor Zhang, the emperor's uncle Ma Fang led them as acting Chariots and Cavalry General and relinquished the command afterward.

sentences.zh: 和帝即位，以舅窦宪为车骑将军，征匈奴，位在公下；

translations.literal: When Emperor He ascended the throne, by his maternal uncle Dou Xian as Chariots and Cavalry General he campaigned against the Xiongnu; his position was below a duke;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He sent his uncle Dou Xian against the Xiongnu as Chariots and Cavalry General, initially below ducal rank;

sentences.zh: 还复有功，迁大将军，位在公上；

translations.literal: after returning he again had merit, was promoted to Grand General, his position above a duke;
translations.idiomatic: further victories raised him to Grand General above the dukes;

sentences.zh: 复征西羌，还免官，罢。

translations.literal: again he campaigned against the Western Qiang; on returning he was dismissed from office and it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: a later western campaign ended with his dismissal and the command's abolition.

sentences.zh: 安帝即位，西羌寇乱，复以舅邓骘为车骑将军征之，还迁大将军，位如宪，数年复罢。

translations.literal: When Emperor An ascended the throne, the Western Qiang raided and rebelled; again by his maternal uncle Deng Zhi as Chariots and Cavalry General he campaigned against them; on returning he was promoted to Grand General, his position like Dou Xian's; after several years it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An likewise used his uncle Deng Zhi to crush Qiang unrest as Chariots and Cavalry General, then as Grand General at Dou's former level until the post lapsed again.

sentences.zh: 自安帝政治衰缺，始以嫡舅耿宝为大将军，常在京都。

translations.literal: From Emperor An, governance declined and lacked; first by his full uncle Geng Bao as Grand General, he constantly was in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: As An's government weakened, Geng Bao—the empress's uncle by blood—held Grand General as a resident capital post.

sentences.zh: 顺帝即位，又以皇后父、兄、弟相继为大将军，如三公焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun ascended the throne, again by the empress's father, elder brother, and younger brother succeeding one another as Grand General, it was like the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Shun continued the pattern, raising the empress's father and brothers in turn to Grand General, coequal with the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 长史、司马皆一人，千石。

translations.literal: Chief clerk and major: each one person, one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One chief clerk and one major, both at one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：司马主兵，如太尉。

translations.literal: Original commentary: the major masters troops, like the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The major commands troops on the model of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 从事中郎二人，六百石。

translations.literal: Gentleman attendants: two persons, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Two gentleman attendants at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：职参谋议，掾属二十九人。

translations.literal: Original commentary: their duty is to counsel plans and discussion; attendants and subordinates: twenty-nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: They counsel on strategy; there are twenty-nine subordinate attendants.

sentences.zh: 令史及御属三十一人。

translations.literal: Clerks and ministerial attendants: thirty-one persons.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-one clerks and ministerial attendants.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：此皆府员职也。

translations.literal: Original commentary: these are all mansion-staff duties.
translations.idiomatic: All belong to the general's household establishment.

sentences.zh: 又赐官骑三十人及鼓吹。

translations.literal: Moreover thirty official riders and drum-and-wind music were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He also receives thirty mounted escorts and a military band.

sentences.zh: 其领军皆有部曲。

translations.literal: Those who lead armies all have divisions and companies.
translations.idiomatic: Every commanding general maintains regimental units.

sentences.zh: 大将军营五部，部校尉一人，比二千石；

translations.literal: The Grand General's camp has five divisions; each division has one colonel, comparable to two thousand bushels;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General's host forms five divisions, each with a colonel at two thousand bushels equivalent;

sentences.zh: 军司马一人，比千石。

translations.literal: army major: one person, comparable to one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: and one army major at one thousand bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 部下有曲，曲有军候一人，比六百石。

translations.literal: Below the division are companies; each company has one army adjutant, comparable to six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Each division breaks into companies, and every company has one adjutant at six hundred bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 曲下有屯，屯长一人，比二百石。

translations.literal: Below the company are platoons; each platoon has one platoon leader, comparable to two hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Companies subdivide into platoons, each led by a platoon chief at two hundred bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 其不置校尉部，但军司马一人。

translations.literal: Where a colonel's division is not established, there is only one army major.
translations.idiomatic: If no colonel heads a division, a single army major holds the command.

sentences.zh: 又有军假司马、假候，皆为副贰。

translations.literal: Moreover there are acting army majors and acting adjutants; all serve as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Acting majors and acting adjutants serve as second-in-command throughout the chain.

sentences.zh: 其别营领属为别部司马，其兵多少各随时宜。

translations.literal: Separate camps under command have separate-division majors; how many troops each has follows timely suitability.
translations.idiomatic: Detached camps answer to detached-division majors, with troop strength adjusted to circumstances.

sentences.zh: 门有门侯。

translations.literal: At gates there are gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: Each gate post has its own gate warden.

sentences.zh: 其余将军，置以征伐，无员职，亦有部曲、司马、军候以领兵。

translations.literal: The remaining generals are established for campaigns; there are no fixed establishment numbers; they also have divisions, majors, and adjutants to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals are named only for active operations, without fixed quotas, yet each still commands through divisions, majors, and adjutants.

sentences.zh: 其职吏部集各一人，总知营事。

translations.literal: Its duty clerk and assembly officer, one each, overall grasp camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One administrative clerk and one mustering officer jointly run the day-to-day business of the encampment.

sentences.zh: 兵曹掾史主兵事器械。

translations.literal: The military bureau attendant masters military affairs, weapons, and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The military bureau's attendants handle arms, armor, and field matériel.

sentences.zh: 禀假掾史主禀假禁司。

translations.literal: The grain-and-leave attendant masters grain rations, temporary leave, and prohibition enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: The supply-and-furlough staff issue rations, regulate leave, and police camp restrictions.

sentences.zh: 又置外刺、刺奸，主罪法。

translations.literal: Moreover outer investigators and inquisition investigators are established, mastering crimes and law.
translations.idiomatic: The command also posts external investigators and internal detectives to enforce military justice.

sentences.zh: 明帝初置度辽将军，以卫南单于众新降有二心者，后数有不安，遂为常守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first established the General Who Crosses the Liao, it was in order to guard the Southern Shanyu's people who had newly surrendered and harbored divided loyalty; afterward there were frequent disturbances, therefore it became a constant garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming first created the General Who Crosses the Liao to watch the newly submitted Southern Shanyu followers, who still wavered in allegiance; recurring unrest soon turned the post into a standing frontier command.
